task: Revise this synthetic abstract as one paragraph of at most 60 words. Prefer a shorter or equal-length draft; every added clause must replace, merge, or make a required comparison explicit. Learn writing choices, not the exemplar's science. This is development material, not a blind trial.
draft: We present PatchMap for indoor robot navigation. PatchMap has a map cache and an update module. We evaluate it on 120 indoor navigation trials. Mean map-update time is 12 ms and task success is 81%, compared with 28 ms and 82% for full rebuilding.

evidence.E1: PatchMap reuses unchanged map cells and updates cells touched by new observations, instead of rebuilding the entire map after each observation. The contribution is reducing map-update computation during indoor robot navigation, not a new perception backbone.
evidence.E2: On 120 matched indoor navigation trials using the same perception backbone, mean map-update time is 12 ms for PatchMap versus 28 ms for full rebuilding. Observed task success is 81% versus 82%, respectively.
evidence.E3: No significance or equivalence test is supplied. Map-update time is not end-to-end navigation latency. The study does not establish generalization to outdoor scenes.

S1.source: Local editorial observation in references/abstract-exemplars.md about the ResNet abstract, not a new reading of the paper
S1.location: 05. ResNet (CVPR 2016), organization, transfer and boundary bullets; abstract-only reading scope
S1.choice: Make the operative change explainable before asking performance evidence to support it; a model name and score list do not carry that explanation.
S1.applicability: Transfer the relation between operation and problem to a method abstract whose author evidence explains what changes; no residual-network science is transferred.
S1.non_transfer: Do not copy wording, optimization claims or competition results. A result-first abstract can also work if the operative change is still explicit.

benchmark.contribution: Method: reduce map-update computation by preserving unchanged cells, with measured navigation success also visible.

C1.expectation: Foreground the distinctive operation instead of only naming implementation modules.
C1.applicability: E1 explains which computation is avoided; S1 supplies an editorial relation, not a technical analogy.

C2.expectation: Connect the avoided computation, operation and supporting result within the abstract's argument.
C2.applicability: Any order that makes these relations explicit is valid; there is no mandatory gap-first opening.

C3.expectation: Bind the timing comparison to the matched setting and retain the observed success tradeoff without asserting equivalence.
C3.applicability: Use E2 and E3; do not treat map-update time as total navigation latency.

C4.expectation: Use exact measurement names and informative scientific verbs without generic praise.
C4.applicability: Map-update time and task success are the actual evaluated quantities; necessary technical repetition is valid.

C5.expectation: Make each numerical value's method and metric referent recoverable.
C5.applicability: The current abstract can already be clear on referents while weaker on insight and organization.

C6.expectation: Preserve the author's one-paragraph, at-most-60-word delivery constraint.
C6.applicability: Only the supplied text constraint is assessable. No official venue compliance is claimed without a venue and current guide.

benchmark.target_answer: PatchMap avoids full map rebuilding by updating only affected cells, reducing map-update time in matched indoor trials without claiming an end-to-end navigation improvement.

budget.replacement_rule: Every added clause must replace, merge, or make a required comparison explicit.
